descriptions.text: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak. Imbues wearer with +1 Dexterity, +1 Constitution, and gives +3 to the skill Double Tap. It's also an anklet. One would think anklets enhance the beauty of feet like toe rings do, but they are excessive, jangly distractions that make you look too garish.

beats.headline: Pried off a dead crawler
beats.text: Three dead crawlers have been left out as a trap where the lemurs caught them: three women of one family, all level 8. Their gear was stripped in a hurry, but the tree-like one still wears an anklet, which takes a few minutes to pry off her ankle, and another still has two rings. The anklet is wood, with three little beads that click like seed pods. Plus one Dexterity, plus one Constitution, plus three to the skill Double Tap, and a description that calls anklets garish. Wood, says Donut: what is this, the 70s? Carl says she needs the constitution. She puts it on her back leg so nobody will see it, and it shrinks into her fur.

beats.headline: The beads rattle
beats.text: Nine city elves are spoiling for a fight, and Carl wants them to make the first move in front of the town guards. On his word Donut lifts her back leg and shakes it, and the anklet's three little beads rattle. The elves come apart. They growl and hiss like a pack of wild animals, the Light Healer claws her own face bloody, the fire mage wets himself and the summoner sucks his thumb. Donut grumbles that she always said wood jewelry was ugly. Salvatore names her the bearer of the forbidden oak, eats an acorn, and begins to glow.

beats.headline: Kept out of sight
beats.text: A single crawler stands in the crowd watching the municipal building fall, and Carl whispers to Donut not to let him see the fallen oak bracelet on her back leg. It is Daniel Bautista, the man who killed the Divider in the swimming pool, and Carl takes him for family of the three dead women they found days ago. Donut picked up the anklet off them. If the man knew, would he want it back? Too bad for him if he did. Carl decides it is best not to broach the subject at all.

relations.note: her city elves take its bearer for the Oak Fell
